In mathematics, '''modular symbols''', introduced independently by [[Bryan John Birch]] and by {{harvs|txt|last=Manin|authorlink=Yuri Manin|year=1972}}, span a [[vector space]] closely related to a space of [[modular form]]s, on which the [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of the [[Hecke algebra]] can be described explicitly.  This makes them useful for computing with spaces of modular forms.

==Definition==

The [[abelian group]] of (universal weight 2) modular symbols is spanned by symbols {α,β} for α, β in the rational projective line '''Q''' ∪ {∞} subject to the relations

* {α,β} + {β,γ} = {α,γ}

Informally, {α,β} represents a homotopy class of paths from α to β in the [[upper half-plane]]. 

The group ''GL''<sub>2</sub>('''Q''') [[Group action (mathematics)|acts]] on the rational [[projective line]], and this induces an action on the modular symbols. 

There is a pairing between cusp forms ''f'' of weight 2 and modular symbols given by integrating the cusp form, or rather ''fd''τ, along the path corresponding to the symbol.
